Ecola State Park, Cannon Beach, Oregon — Coastal Scenes

Twilight (2008)

Ecola State Park on the Oregon coast is an important part of the first film's Pacific Northwest production footprint. Indian Beach provided coastal material associated with the story's La Push setting. The park is a real public destination, but it should not be confused with First Beach in La Push, Washington.

La Push, Washington — First Beach

Twilight (2008)

First Beach at La Push is the real-world beach Stephenie Meyer set the Quileute legend scenes at. It was used for establishing location photography and is the canonical setting for the beach scenes in the novel, though the film's beach scenes were shot primarily in Oregon.

  • First Beach — Bella and Jacob, Quileute legends scene (novel setting)
  • Quileute Reservation — wolf pack territory

Twilight (2008) · Story Setting

First Beach is the real-world setting behind the Quileute beach scenes in Stephenie Meyer's story. It is important to distinguish the real place from the movie production: the beach material in the first film was shot primarily in Oregon, including Ecola State Park, rather than at First Beach itself.

  • Novel setting — Bella and Jacob's beach conversation and Quileute legends
  • Real-world La Push coastline — the landscape that inspired the story's beach setting
